prompt:
A densely annotated editorial infographic plate, drawn by hand in confident ink
line with light watercolour and gouache wash on bright warm-white paper.
Contour line varies in weight and is charcoal near-black. Dimensional but not
photographic: restrained hatching, subtle texture, believable volume, selective
shadow, clean uncluttered background. Every material reads as itself — dull grey
lead, unglazed earthenware, weathered timber, damp fibrous bark — and materials
that differ in the explanation look visibly different. Quiet palette of stone,
clay, wood, and metal tones over the warm-white ground, with one or two
desaturated accents that each keep a single meaning throughout the plate.
Contemporary editorial typography: one calm display face for the title, one
highly legible face for the many small labels, sentence case, crisply printed
and correctly spelled. Annotation is dense and disciplined — leader lines,
brackets, dimension marks, magnified inset circles, small side studies — laid
out so no two leaders cross. Asymmetric composition with about a quarter of the
page left quiet. Modern printing on clean stock: fresh, crisp, and unaged. The
only lettering anywhere on the plate is the title, the deck, the labels, and the
short notes. The words hero, drawing, figure, plate, inset, zone, band, strip,
trio, column, and cutaway describe the construction of the page and are never
lettered onto it, alone or in a phrase: no headings that name parts of the
layout, no percentages or
proportions of the page, no tags in brackets after a label or note, no sentence
describing the drawing or explaining what the reader is meant to see, no
signature, monogram, date, watermark, or credit line.

The plate is headed "bookgen", with the standing line "Reads a finished book's own essays back and dresses it in a jacket: a back-cover blurb and a designed, painted front." beneath it.

The dominant picture, filling roughly half the page, shows A book jacket unfolded flat, back cover on the left and front cover on the right, with the finished manuscript lying beneath it: a stack of draft2 essay pages and one Plan sheet. The blurb path rises from the full essays and the Plan through a text model and settles as lines of type on the back cover. The cover path starts from the Plan, the blurb lifted off the back cover, and short clipped essay pages. These three meet at a text model, which writes one cover design sheet. The cover design sheet then passes to an image model, which paints the front cover. The front cover shows a title and an author byline. Every arrow points upward from the manuscript toward the jacket, and one arrow runs from the back cover into the cover design.

Magnified circles set beside it show circle one sets whole essay pages beside clipped excerpt pages, showing that the blurb reads everything while the cover reads excerpts. Circle two shows the Plan's top heading lifting off to become the title. Circle three shows a JPEG re-encoded into front-cover.png rather than renamed. has four studies. The first is a printed prompt with no spending. The second is the chain halted at the design sheet with a blank canvas. The third is an existing file left untouched unless forced. The fourth is a two-position dial marked cheap and pro.

Colour is used so that Ink blue marks everything the text model writes. Madder red marks everything the image model paints. Ochre marks files written into the book folder.

Draw these quantities as dimension marks or counts: 2 subcommands, blurb and cover. 2 steps in the cover chain, design then paint. 3 inputs to the cover design: Plan, blurb, excerpts. 3 files written. 2 spend tiers, cheap and pro.

These trade words appear on the plate, each set against the thing it names: blurb on the back-cover path. cover on the front-cover path. Plan on the manuscript's top sheet. draft2 essays on the page stack. cover design document on the sheet between the models. back-cover-blurb.md and front-cover.png on the output files. --dry-run on the printed-prompt study. --prompt-only on the halted chain. --force on the untouched-file study. cheap and pro on the dial. title and author byline on the front cover.

Letter these words onto the drawings, spelled exactly as given: Plan, draft2 essays, blurb, cover, text model, image model, cover design, back cover, front cover, title, author byline. full essays, essay excerpts, Plan heading, re-encoded to PNG. --dry-run, --prompt-only, --force, cheap, pro. book folder, back-cover-blurb.md, cover design document, front-cover.png. after the mill, blurb step, cover step, finished jacket.

Set these short notes beside what they explain: Drawn from what the book actually says; The cover reads the blurb first. Blurb reads whole essays, cover reads excerpts; No title given? The Plan heading supplies it; A JPEG is re-encoded, not renamed. Prints the prompt, spends nothing; Stops after the design, no painting; Existing files are kept unless forced. All three land in the book folder.
